Let \( ABC \) be an isosceles triangle with \( AB = AC \). Points \( P \) and \( Q \) are located inside triangle \( ABC \) such that \( BP = PQ = QC \). Suppose that \( \angle BAP = 20^\circ \), \( \angle PAQ = 46^\circ \), and \( \angle QAC = 26^\circ \). Compute the measure of \( \angle APC \) in degrees.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let all angles be in degrees. Since \(P,Q\) are inside the triangle, the rays from \(A\) occur in the order  
\[
AB,\; AP,\; AQ,\; AC.
\]
Hence
\[
\angle BAC=20^\circ+46^\circ+26^\circ=92^\circ.
\]
Because \(AB=AC\), the base angles are
\[
\angle ABC=\angle BCA=\frac{180^\circ-92^\circ}{2}=44^\circ.
\]

Normalize the triangle by setting
\[
AB=AC=1.
\]
Let
\[
AP=x,\qquad AQ=y.
\]

Using the Law of Cosines in triangles \(ABP\), \(APQ\), and \(AQC\), we get
\[
BP^2=1+x^2-2x\cos20^\circ,
\]
\[
PQ^2=x^2+y^2-2xy\cos46^\circ,
\]
\[
QC^2=y^2+1-2y\cos26^\circ.
\]
Since \(BP=PQ=QC\), we have the two equations
\[
1-2x\cos20^\circ=y^2-2xy\cos46^\circ \tag{1}
\]
and
\[
x^2-2xy\cos46^\circ=1-2y\cos26^\circ. \tag{2}
\]

We now find the positive solution of these equations. Write \(s_k=\sin k^\circ\). The solution is
\[
x=\frac{s_{34}}{s_{74}},\qquad y=\frac{s_{40}}{s_{74}}.
\]

Check equation (2). Multiplying by \(s_{74}^2\), it becomes
\[
s_{34}^2-2s_{40}s_{34}\cos46^\circ
=
s_{74}^2-2s_{40}s_{74}\cos26^\circ.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
s_{34}^2-s_{74}^2+2s_{40}\bigl(s_{74}\cos26^\circ-s_{34}\cos46^\circ\bigr)=0.
\]
Now
\[
s_{74}^2-s_{34}^2
=\sin(74+34)\sin(74-34)
=s_{108}s_{40}=s_{72}s_{40},
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
s_{74}\cos26^\circ-s_{34}\cos46^\circ
&=\frac12\bigl(s_{100}+s_{48}-s_{80}+s_{12}\bigr)\\
&=\frac12\bigl(s_{80}+s_{48}-s_{80}+s_{12}\bigr)\\
&=\frac12(s_{48}+s_{12})\\
&=\frac12\cdot 2\sin30^\circ\cos18^\circ\\
&=\frac{s_{72}}{2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus
\[
s_{34}^2-s_{74}^2+2s_{40}\bigl(s_{74}\cos26^\circ-s_{34}\cos46^\circ\bigr)
=
-s_{72}s_{40}+s_{72}s_{40}=0.
\]
So (2) holds.

Check equation (1). Multiplying by \(s_{74}^2\), it becomes
\[
s_{74}^2-2s_{34}s_{74}\cos20^\circ
=
s_{40}^2-2s_{40}s_{34}\cos46^\circ.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
s_{74}^2-s_{40}^2-2s_{34}\bigl(s_{74}\cos20^\circ-s_{40}\cos46^\circ\bigr)=0.
\]
Now
\[
s_{74}^2-s_{40}^2
=\sin(74+40)\sin(74-40)
=s_{114}s_{34}=s_{66}s_{34},
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
s_{74}\cos20^\circ-s_{40}\cos46^\circ
&=\frac12\bigl(s_{94}+s_{54}-s_{86}+s_{6}\bigr)\\
&=\frac12\bigl(s_{86}+s_{54}-s_{86}+s_{6}\bigr)\\
&=\frac12(s_{54}+s_{6})\\
&=\frac12\cdot 2\sin30^\circ\cos24^\circ\\
&=\frac{s_{66}}{2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus
\[
s_{74}^2-s_{40}^2-2s_{34}\bigl(s_{74}\cos20^\circ-s_{40}\cos46^\circ\bigr)
=
s_{66}s_{34}-s_{66}s_{34}=0.
\]
So (1) holds.

Therefore the interior configuration has
\[
\frac{AP}{AC}=x=\frac{\sin34^\circ}{\sin74^\circ}.
\]

Now consider triangle \(APC\). We have
\[
\angle PAC=\angle PAQ+\angle QAC=46^\circ+26^\circ=72^\circ.
\]
Let \(\angle ACP=\alpha\). Then
\[
\angle APC=180^\circ-72^\circ-\alpha=108^\circ-\alpha.
\]
By the Law of Sines in \(\triangle APC\),
\[
\frac{AP}{AC}=\frac{\sin\alpha}{\sin(108^\circ-\alpha)}.
\]
But
\[
\frac{AP}{AC}=\frac{\sin34^\circ}{\sin74^\circ}.
\]
Since \(\alpha=34^\circ\) gives exactly this ratio and \(0<\alpha<44^\circ\) because \(P\) is inside the triangle, we get
\[
\alpha=34^\circ.
\]
Hence
\[
\angle APC=108^\circ-34^\circ=74^\circ.
\]

\[
\boxed{74}
\]
